slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 19, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led the major U.S. indexes, closing up 1.1% at 26,430.89 after a 290.85-point gain.
The S&P 500 rose 0.4% to 7,691.39 (+31.95), and the Russell 2000 added 0.3% to 2,728.30.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.1% to 51,966.03 (-36.38), so the session’s strength sat in growth and smaller-cap indexes rather than the 30-stock average.

The day’s main U.S. data print in the calendar was the NAHB Housing Market Index for October: 29 actual, below the 32 estimate and down from 32 prior.
That reading landed at 2:00 p.m.
ET in the file — a gauge of home-builder confidence, not a jobs or inflation number.

Implied volatility eased: the VIX fell 7.8% to 18.44 (-1.55), with an intraday low of 17.39 in the quote.
That sat alongside higher equity indexes, consistent with a quieter fear gauge on the close.

Sector performance on the Nasdaq list was uneven.
Consumer Cyclical averaged +2.3%, the best group in the file.
Utilities averaged -3.4%, the weakest.
Real Estate -1.7%, Financial Services -0.9%, and Industrials -0.9% also lagged.
Healthcare was essentially flat (0.0%), while Basic Materials +0.9% and Consumer Defensive +0.9% posted modest gains.

Amazon was the standout megacap percentage mover: $AMZN +5.0% to 262.45 on 54.7M shares in the injected quote.
That helped anchor the consumer-cyclical strength even as several other mega names moved less than 2%.

Semiconductor and large-tech names mostly closed green in the file after a week commentators had described as rough for AI-linked stocks.:
- $AMD +1.8%
- $AVGO +1.8%
- $NVDA +1.4%
- $INTC +2.4%
- $MSFT +0.8%
- $NFLX -1.0% to 69.85

Cleveland-Cliffs dominated single-name steel headlines: $CLF +16.3% to 14.10 after Q3 EPS of $0.28 vs $0.21 estimated and revenue of $5.61B vs $5.69B estimated.
$STLD rose 1.9% to 245.17 with EPS $5.26 vs $5.48 est. and revenue above the revenue estimate.

Financials were a drag among large banks in the tape: $JPM -1.8% to 333.53.
The session also carried a cluster of bank earnings with actuals — including Fifth Third ($FITB EPS $1.13 vs $0.83 est.), Zions ($ZION EPS $1.78 vs $1.64 est.), and Western Alliance ($WAL EPS $2.45 vs $2.42 est.) — with mixed stock reactions versus those lines.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-10-16) showed the 10-year at 5.1% and the 2s10s spread at 0.35 percentage points.
Bill auctions on Oct. 19 printed 3-month at 4.1% and 6-month at 4.2% in the economic calendar.

Cross-asset closes from the file: gold futures (GC) +0.1% to 4,162.80; Brent crude +0.5% to 110.08; the dollar proxy $UUP +0.3% to 29.00; Bitcoin roughly flat at 81,824.78 (0.0%).
Overseas indexes in the same payload were mostly lower ahead or alongside the U.S. session — Nikkei 225 -0.6%, FTSE 100 -1.1%, Hang Seng -0.8%.
